nodes.description: Newly recognized in 2026. Autoimmunity and systemic inflammation were identified as previously under-recognized features of the RNU4ATAC spectrum, with immunological investigation showing enhanced HLA-DR and PD-1 expression on patient T cells - a pattern of T-cell activation and exhaustion. This matters clinically because the older picture of Roifman syndrome was a pure antibody deficiency, which would not predict autoimmunity.

nodes.description: RNU4ATAC encodes U4atac, a non-protein-coding snRNA of the minor spliceosome. Roifman syndrome arises from compound heterozygous variants in which at least one allele spares the 5' stem-loop - typically one variant at the 5' stem-loop or the Sm-binding element and the second in stem II. This genotype rule is what separates Roifman syndrome from MOPD I: variants located exclusively in the 5' stem-loop give the severe lethal MOPD I phenotype, because that region is where U4atac binds the essential di-snRNP proteins.

nodes.description: U4atac base-pairs U6atac and licenses it to catalyse excision of U12-type minor introns, which occur in roughly 750 human genes. Destabilizing U4atac causes intron retention and elevated alternative splicing in that gene set, shifting the tissue-specific distribution of mRNA isoforms. Because the affected gene set is small but functionally clustered, the downstream consequences are selective rather than global - which is why one snRNA lesion produces an immune, a skeletal and a ciliary phenotype rather than generalized cell failure.

nodes.description: The best-resolved arm of the mechanism. B-cell numbers are dramatically reduced and differentiation halts at the transitional B-cell stage. The block is not a shortage of survival signal: B-cell activating factor (BAFF) is abundantly available, yet development past the BAFF-dependent stage is crippled, because minor splicing of MAPK1 - the critical signalling component downstream of BAFF - is disturbed. So the cell has the ligand and lacks the ability to transduce it.

nodes.description: Cilium assembly is over-represented among minor-intron-containing genes: 86 cilium-related genes carry at least one minor intron, 23 of them ciliopathy-related. Primary cilium function is altered in patient fibroblasts and a u4atac zebrafish model shows ciliopathy-related traits, so ciliary dysfunction is a genuine downstream mechanism rather than a coincidental overlap. This is the arm that plausibly explains the skeletal, retinal and neurodevelopmental features that a purely haematopoietic mechanism cannot.
